text:
Provisional cross-functional app delivery process

Because the platform is unidentified, this is a generic working view rather than a confirmed platform-specific process. The arrow labels show each handoff.

Actors, steps, and handoffs
flowchart LR
  subgraph BU[Business user]
    A[Define need and success criteria]
    H[Review and accept outcome]
  end
  subgraph AD[Architect or developer]
    B[Design solution]
    C[Build and configure app]
    F[Review test results and approve release]
  end
  subgraph PF[Platform]
    D[Validate package and dependencies]
    E[Build and test deployment artifact]
    G[Deploy and configure release]
    J[Collect status and telemetry]
  end
  subgraph RT[Runtime]
    I[Start and run application]
    K[Serve users and emit health data]
  end

  A -->|Requirements and acceptance criteria| B
  B -->|Architecture and technical specification| C
  C -->|Source, configuration, and dependencies| D
  D -->|Validated application package| E
  E -->|Test results and deployable artifact| F
  F -->|Approved release| G
  G -->|Application image, configuration, and secrets references| I
  I -->|Running application endpoint| H
  I -->|Runtime status and logs| J
  H -->|Usage and feedback| K
  K -->|Requests, metrics, logs, and alerts| J
  J -->|Operational feedback and incidents| C

issues: The platform-specific workflow cannot be verified because the platform is unidentified.
The diagram invents platform responsibilities, release controls, artifacts, and handoffs not established by the context.
The sequence from business feedback to the runtime serving users is logically unclear.

limitations: The platform name, installed components, release controls, and runtime architecture were not supplied, so exact steps and handoffs cannot be verified.
